1	# R079 — **E01/E02 step 3: the timed chip's ink is the calendar colour at HALF VALUE — settled by measurement, not guessed.**
2	The standing question was "is the ref's dark same-hue ink a *translation* of the calendar colour, or the colour at some alpha?" It is a
3	translation with **one parameter**: the ink is the chip's own colour **moved halfway to its pole** — half to black in light, half to white
4	in dark — **hue and saturation untouched**. Measured 1:1 on the ref as ink **cores** (the extreme cluster, *not* AA edges): red bar
5	(235,76,70) → ink **(117,37,34)**; blue bar (59,134,247) → **(26,67,123)**; an olive chip (254,204,0) → **(127,102,0)** — **1:2 on every
6	channel of all three**. Halving RGB *is* halving the HSV value, because `S = (max−min)/max` is invariant under a uniform scale, so no
7	colour-space round trip and no per-colour fudge is needed; a separate "saturation/value mapping" is **not**. R078's quoted (99,131,172) was
8	an AA pixel — the cores are what settle it. (2026-10-17)
9	
10	## 本轮 (R079)
11	Atomic step: **E01/E02 step 3 — `timedChip`'s Label `color:` `AppTheme.text` → a derived `inkColor`.** Edit
12	(`apps/calendar/qml/CalendarScheduleView.qml:626-646` + the Label): `readonly property color inkColor` = `c + (pole − c) * 0.5` with
13	`pole = AppTheme.dark ? 1 : 0`. Evidence: `docs/ui-calendar/r079-ink-light.png`, `r079-ink-dark.png`, `r079-ink-compare.png`
14	(ref blue chip | ours, both ×3 NEAREST).
15	**How it was verified — a coverage model was needed, and the numbers are the proof.** A pixelSize-9 glyph never reaches full coverage,
16	so each chip was tested by **solving the blend's coverage per channel**: `t = (fill − pixel) / (fill − predicted ink)`. A correct ink makes
17	the three t's **agree**; a wrong one cannot.
18	- **Light:** green bar (57,196,135) → ink (28,98,67): darkest pixel (45,111,85) ⇒ t = 0.91/0.91/0.89. Gold (215,166,44) → (107,83,22):
19	  (129,105,43) ⇒ 0.84/0.86/0.89. Blue (48,140,198) → (24,70,99): (49,89,121) ⇒ 0.87/0.88/0.85.

21	  (151,197,226): (137,183,206) ⇒ 0.88/0.89/0.85.
22	**Nine chip readings, both legs, t agreeing to ±0.05 inside each pixel ⇒ the assumed endpoint is the ink.** Corroboration by kind: R078's

24	idiom, and the ×3 composite puts the ref's "Stretchin…" ink beside our "Morning planning" — same dark same-hue ink on a light same-hue wash.
25	**Regression guard (measures, not assumptions).** The bars read **bit-identically to R078 in both legs** — light and dark both

82	- **THE REF'S INK RULE IS ONE PARAMETER: HALFWAY TO THE POLE (R079).** Verified on **three** ref colours (red, blue, olive) as 1:2 on
83	  every channel, and on **nine** of our chips in both legs by the coverage test. ⇒ **any future "same-hue text/tint" on a chip is
84	  `c + (pole − c) * 0.5`, never a typed hex and never an alpha.** Corollary: the *dark* leg is the ref's rule mirrored, not a ref

87	  (blue R read 60 where the ink is 24); in *dark* the brightest pixel overshot (blue G reached the ink's G while R/B sat below it —
88	  impossible for a convex blend). Small coloured text is subpixel-AA'd, so a single pixel is off the fill→ink segment in **both** themes.
89	  **The test that works: assume the ink, then check `t = (fill − pixel)/(fill − ink)` agrees across the three channels of one pixel.**
90	  Expect ±0.05; a wrong endpoint spreads t by 0.2+.

# R079 — **E01/E02 step 3: the timed chip's ink is the calendar colour at HALF VALUE — settled by measurement, not guessed.**
The standing question was "is the ref's dark same-hue ink a *translation* of the calendar colour, or the colour at some alpha?" It is a
translation with **one parameter**: the ink is the chip's own colour **moved halfway to its pole** — half to black in light, half to white
in dark — **hue and saturation untouched**. Measured 1:1 on the ref as ink **cores** (the extreme cluster, *not* AA edges): red bar
(235,76,70) → ink **(117,37,34)**; blue bar (59,134,247) → **(26,67,123)**; an olive chip (254,204,0) → **(127,102,0)** — **1:2 on every
channel of all three**. Halving RGB *is* halving the HSV value, because `S = (max−min)/max` is invariant under a uniform scale, so no
colour-space round trip and no per-colour fudge is needed; a separate "saturation/value mapping" is **not**. R078's quoted (99,131,172) was
an AA pixel — the cores are what settle it. (2026-10-17)

## 本轮 (R079)
Atomic step: **E01/E02 step 3 — `timedChip`'s Label `color:` `AppTheme.text` → a derived `inkColor`.** Edit
(`apps/calendar/qml/CalendarScheduleView.qml:626-646` + the Label): `readonly property color inkColor` = `c + (pole − c) * 0.5` with
`pole = AppTheme.dark ? 1 : 0`. Evidence: `docs/ui-calendar/r079-ink-light.png`, `r079-ink-dark.png`, `r079-ink-compare.png`
(ref blue chip | ours, both ×3 NEAREST).
**How it was verified — a coverage model was needed, and the numbers are the proof.** A pixelSize-9 glyph never reaches full coverage,
so each chip was tested by **solving the blend's coverage per channel**: `t = (fill − pixel) / (fill − predicted ink)`. A correct ink makes
the three t's **agree**; a wrong one cannot.
- **Light:** green bar (57,196,135) → ink (28,98,67): darkest pixel (45,111,85) ⇒ t = 0.91/0.91/0.89. Gold (215,166,44) → (107,83,22):
  (129,105,43) ⇒ 0.84/0.86/0.89. Blue (48,140,198) → (24,70,99): (49,89,121) ⇒ 0.87/0.88/0.85.
- **Dark:** green → (156,226,195): (141,210,176) ⇒ 0.87/0.88/0.85. Gold → (235,211,150): (220,199,128) ⇒ 0.89/0.91/0.81. Blue →
  (151,197,226): (137,183,206) ⇒ 0.88/0.89/0.85.
**Nine chip readings, both legs, t agreeing to ±0.05 inside each pixel ⇒ the assumed endpoint is the ink.** Corroboration by kind: R078's
grey ink produced near-equal channels; every chip now reads **its own hue** (blue B>G>R, green G>B>R, gold R>G>B), which is the ref's
idiom, and the ×3 composite puts the ref's "Stretchin…" ink beside our "Morning planning" — same dark same-hue ink on a light same-hue wash.
**Regression guard (measures, not assumptions).** The bars read **bit-identically to R078 in both legs** — light and dark both
(48,140,198) blue / (57,196,135) green / (215,166,44) gold; dark fills (36,69,90) / (40,90,68) / (96,79,35) also unchanged.
**Not touched:** the fill alpha, `radius: 5`, the R077 bar, the R078 border deletion, and the **whole all-day band** (its chip ink is
still grey — an *unmeasured* question, see 外推).

## E01/E02 status (tester's call, R079)
**`Chip carries a saturated same-hue bar at its left edge` — PASS** (R077). **`Chip has no border/ring` — PASS** (R078).
**`Chip text is dark same-hue` — now PASS**, light + dark, on the t-agreement evidence above (timed chip, the only family the ref anchors
it on). **Do not read this as "the chip language is done": the band chip's ink is grey and the ref has not been measured for it.**

## 仍差 (top 8, visual-impact order)
1. **The all-day BAND chip's ink is still `AppTheme.text` (grey) while the timed chip's is hue.** **Unmeasured in the ref** — but the band
   chip is the *same* chip family, and R079 showed a crop of the *timed* chip is enough to settle an ink. **Next round #1: measure the ref's
   band-chip ink core first (one crop, the same t-agreement test), then copy `inkColor` if the ref says hue — or record that it is grey and
   leave it.**
2. **The all-day BAND chip's icon — ours has NONE.** Four 12×12 blobs at x247-258 / 329-340 / 491-502 / 654-665 ⇒ ~4 ref px inside each
   column rule, on an 18-ref-px row ⇒ ours ~15 px at ×1.33, ~5 px in. Ring-shaped (hollow centres), *coloured per calendar*. Needs a ruling
   on the icon's source/shape before it can be built — **do not start it without one.**
3. **A02 — band expansion / shared bottom edge.** The band's height is a fixed 76; the ref grows it with the number of all-day rows and
   shares the bottom edge with the 2px `allDaySeparator`. **Never reviewed. Needs a fixture with 1 and 4 all-day rows to be measurable at
   all** — do not start without deciding that first.
4. **Ref gutter labels are 12-hour and two-tone** (dark hour number + smaller lighter `AM`/`PM`), right-aligned on the **suffix's** right
   edge (digit (89,89,89), suffix (176..193)); ours is single-size 24-hour `07:00`. **Needs ruling F.**
5. **Dim snaps while the card animates** (`KosWorkspaceDialog.qml:24-27`): `Overlay.modal` is a plain un-animated `Rectangle`. **R058
   re-confirmed both directions.** App-wide. **Needs ruling A.**
6. **Shadow magnitude** (D03 follow-up): peak Δ≈10/255 = 3.9%; macOS alerts read ~Δ25–40 at 1px. Touching
   `KosSurface.effectiveElevation` / the `0.38` factor is **app-wide**. **Needs ruling B.**
7. **`slice(0, 2)` per cell drops a 3rd item with no `+N`** (R048; R076 proved R072's "aim it at the band" wrong — Apr 2 carries exactly 2
   all-day items). The month day cell holds 1 chip + `N` where the ref stacks 3. **Needs ruling D — and needs a 3-all-day-item day before
   the band half can be reproduced at all.**
8. **Ref band chips are inset ~2 ref-px from their column rule; ours sit at inset 1** (R076: Thu chip 489..567 in a 487..569 column).
   ~3.7 px at our scale ⇒ near-identical; **do not chase it without a ruling** — it rides on ruling G (the spec's "inset 2–3" is the same
   number read in ref px).
- *Cosmetic, no ID:* the band's empty third slot is visibly ruled (R074's separators cross it) — **ruling D, do not patch.**
  `secondary` hover = neutral grey 79 no edge; `flat` hover = accent tint (35,60,81) **with** a 1px edge. D02 radius **16** vs
  spec 24/32 — **keep 16**. Topmost visible gutter label is **half-clipped** when a scroll offset lands an hour line exactly on
  the viewport top (R066; scroll artifact, not a form defect).

## 最近已改 (most recent 8)
1. R079 — **E01/E02 step 3**: `timedChip` Label `color:` `AppTheme.text` → derived **`inkColor`** = the calendar colour halfway to its
   pole (light: half to black; dark: half to white), hue+saturation untouched (`CalendarScheduleView.qml:626-646` + Label). Nothing else.
2. R078 — **E01/E02 step 2**: `timedChip`'s `border.width: 1` + `border.color: withAlpha(itemColor, 0.34)` **deleted**, replaced by a
   comment carrying the three-edge measurement. Nothing else touched.
3. R077 — **E01/E02 step 1**: `timedChip` gained a saturated same-hue left bar — derived `stripeWidth`/`stripeInset` (= 4, from
   `chipHeight/4`), capsule `radius: width/2`, vertical margin 2, `color: itemColor(modelData)`; Label `leftMargin` 5 → 13.
4. R076 — **A03**: `allDayChip`'s `radius` → four corner radii, square where `allDayContinues(item, columnDate, ±1)`; new injected
   `itemRecord` on the view (bound in `Main.qml`'s two `CalendarScheduleView`s) + `isoDay` / `isoDayPattern` / `lastCoveredDay` /
   `allDayContinues`. Single-day chips bit-identical to R075.
5. R075 — **A01 step 5**: `allDayChip` `radius: 5` → `Math.round(root.allDayRowHeight / 3)` = **8** (ref r≈6 on an 18px row).
6. R074 — **A01 step 4**: the band's `allDayColumn` gained the grid's column separators (1px `gridLine` left edge + right rim on the last
   column); y=215 = 237 at 52/202/352/502/652/802, identical to the grid; boundaries single-width.
7. R073 — **A01 step 3**: `allDayBandInset` 3 → **1**; band 80 → **76** (derived); separator 236/237 → **232/233**, first hour line
   238 → **234**. Verified the gap stayed 1.
8. R072 — **A01 step 2**: row 18→**24**, gap 2→**1**, band 48→**80**, all derived from four new tokens; the band's `ColumnLayout`
   re-anchored to stop surplus spreading into the spacings.

## 外推待确认 (live only — the older live items and the settled R070/R072 notes are archived to rounds.md tail)
- **THE REF'S INK RULE IS ONE PARAMETER: HALFWAY TO THE POLE (R079).** Verified on **three** ref colours (red, blue, olive) as 1:2 on
  every channel, and on **nine** of our chips in both legs by the coverage test. ⇒ **any future "same-hue text/tint" on a chip is
  `c + (pole − c) * 0.5`, never a typed hex and never an alpha.** Corollary: the *dark* leg is the ref's rule mirrored, not a ref
  measurement — the ref image has no dark mode, so dark chip colours are **extrapolation** and must be labelled as such.
- **AN INK CAN ONLY BE MEASURED BY THE COVERAGE TEST (R079) — not by its hull in either theme.** In *light* the darkest pixel overshot
  (blue R read 60 where the ink is 24); in *dark* the brightest pixel overshot (blue G reached the ink's G while R/B sat below it —
  impossible for a convex blend). Small coloured text is subpixel-AA'd, so a single pixel is off the fill→ink segment in **both** themes.
  **The test that works: assume the ink, then check `t = (fill − pixel)/(fill − ink)` agrees across the three channels of one pixel.**
  Expect ±0.05; a wrong endpoint spreads t by 0.2+.
- **A CROSS-ROUND PNG IS NOT POSITION-ALIGNED (R079).** r078-noborder-light.png vs r079-ink-light.png in the same session, same view, same
  date: R078 has 16px bands at 277-292 / 414-430 / 517-532 where R079 has none, and R079 has 454-470 / 477-492 / 557-572 where R078 has
  none; in the dark pair, y317-332 is a **green** chip in R078 (mean (66,110,91)) and a **blue** one in R079 (mean (46,80,102)). ⇒ **never
  A/B two rounds' captures pixel-for-pixel; re-derive the band map on every capture.** The R071 column map and the R073 y-map are the only
  cross-round invariants that have held, and they are *layout* maps, not content maps.
- **THE LAUNCHER REFUSES WHEN A LIVED INSTANCE IS ALIVE (R079), AND `>/dev/null` HIDES IT.** `start-review-vm.sh` exits **1** with
  `Owned review instance still running: <pid>` if `live-app.pid` still points at a running `kos-calendar` — so a fresh `light` launch
  silently produces **no new process**, and the *old* (e.g. dark) app answers the capture. **Cost R079 one whole wasted capture.** ⇒
  **`kill "$(cat live-app.pid)"` first, and never discard the launcher's stderr** (`nohup ./start-review-vm.sh light 2>&1 | head -2 &`).
  A correct relaunch gives a **new pid in `live-app.pid`** — check it. (Corollary: an old app still watching the shared
  `harness/command.json` will happily serve a capture list aimed at a new app.)
- **A CHIP EDGE CAN ONLY PROVE "NO BORDER" IF IT DOES NOT ABUT A RULE (R078).** The left edge sits on the column rule and R077 mis-read
  a 1px border there; a **top or bottom** edge — or, better, two of them on two chips — carries the answer. **Idiom: read the RAW profile
  across the edge and check monotonicity** — a real border is a row darker *and* more saturated than the fill; a corner/AA row is *lighter*.
  Ours has neither, so on a chip whose fill is a light wash, **an AA transition and no-transition are the same verdict.**
- **THE REF'S SAME-HUE LEFT STRIPE IS A TIMED-GRID-CHIP PROPERTY, AND THE BAND CHIP HAS AN ICON INSTEAD (R077).** R073's
  "x=491-493 = (187,62,216) stripe" is the **band icon's left arc** (ring, hollow centre x495-496). ⇒ **never cite the ref for
  a stripe in the all-day band**, and never read a saturated 3px run without checking it is constant-width top-to-bottom.
  Corollary: **the band's chips do have a coloured element — a ~12×12 per-calendar ring icon ~4 px inside their column rule.**
- **THE REF BAR IS AN ABSOLUTE STROKE, NOT A FRACTION OF THE CHIP (R077).** 2.4 ref px on an 11 ref px 30-min chip *and* on a
  22 ref px 60-min chip. ⇒ ours stays `chipHeight/4` = 4 on the fixed 16 px chip **regardless of duration**. The horizontal
  scale is the one to use for its width (×1.85 on the column); the ink envelope is ~2.4 px, not the 3 px it reads at its thinnest.
- **OUR `timedChip` GEOMETRY AFTER R079 (light 1100x692):** chip = column + 3 (Container `anchors.margins: 3`), so Thu =
  **505..648**; **fill 505-508, bar 509-512** (4 px, capsule), text ink from **518**. Light fill `(216,234,245)`, dark fill `(36,69,90)`,
  bar `(48,140,198)` in both legs — all **unchanged by R079**; light ink `(24,70,99)`, dark ink `(151,197,226)` for that blue chip.
  **No border pixel at any edge, light or dark.** The Label's `leftMargin` is derived (`inset + width + 5`) — do not retype 13 if either
  token moves. **Our chip calendar colours are NOT the ref's**: ours blue **(48,140,198)** / green **(57,196,135)** / gold **(215,166,44)**
  (read off the bars, which are `itemColor` with no alpha), the ref's blue is (59,134,247) — so **our ink is the same *rule* on a
  different source**, and its magnitude must never be compared to the ref's hex directly.
- **THE REFERENCE WEEK CONTAINS NO MULTI-DAY ALL-DAY EVENT (R076).** Measured, not assumed: all 21 band rows carry the column
  rule unbroken with chip fills on both sides, and every chip's fill is inset 1–2 px inside **one** column. ⇒ **A03's clause
  has no ref anchor; the ref can only anchor single-day all-day chips.** Corollary: **a claim that "the ref does X for
  multi-day strips" cannot be made from this image** — say "spec-only" instead.
- **ALL-DAY RANGE ARITHMETIC SUBTRACTS EXACTLY ONE DAY — NEVER TWO (R076).** The ICS carries `DTEND;VALUE=DATE:20260403` for
  `Multi-day review`, the record's end is the **inclusive last day (Apr 2)**, and the popover proves the truth: it prints
  **`2026年3月30日星期一 – 2026年4月1日星期三`**. `Main.qml:itemDetailsRange` and the new `lastCoveredDay` both subtract one day
  and **agree with the popover** ⇒ the model is consistent; any new range math must subtract one day and be checked against
  that popover string. **Corollary: the corner rule and the column membership use *different* sources (record `start`/`end`
  vs the service's date expansion) — they agree today, so any future all-day membership change must be re-checked against the
  corners. Second corollary: R072's "Thursday carries 3 all-day items" is WRONG — Apr 2 holds exactly 2 (`Design sync`,
  `Release notes`); nothing is hidden by `slice(0, 2)` on this fixture.**
- **A SQUARE JOINT ONLY READS AS "ONE BAR" BECAUSE THE COLUMN RULE IS DRAWN THROUGH THE BAND (R074 + R076).** The ref does the
  same (its rule is unbroken through every band row). ⇒ **if the R074 separators are ever removed, A03's rendering collapses
  back into "one pill per day". The two changes are a pair.**
- **`itemRecord` IS A NEW INJECTED PROPERTY ON `CalendarScheduleView` (R076), bound in `Main.qml`'s two schedule views
  (`itemAllDay:`/`itemRecord:`/`itemHour:` neighbours). A view that omits it gets `({})` ⇒ `continuesLeft/Right` false ⇒ every
  chip fully rounded (falls back to the R075 shape, no crash, no binding error).** Any *new* schedule-view instance must bind

# R079 — **E01/E02 step 3: the timed chip's ink is the calendar colour at HALF VALUE — settled by measurement, not guessed.**
The standing question was "is the ref's dark same-hue ink a *translation* of the calendar colour, or the colour at some alpha?" It is a
translation with **one parameter**: the ink is the chip's own colour **moved halfway to its pole** — half to black in light, half to white
in dark — **hue and saturation untouched**. Measured 1:1 on the ref as ink **cores** (the extreme cluster, *not* AA edges): red bar
(235,76,70) → ink **(117,37,34)**; blue bar (59,134,247) → **(26,67,123)**; an olive chip (254,204,0) → **(127,102,0)** — **1:2 on every
channel of all three**. Halving RGB *is* halving the HSV value, because `S = (max−min)/max` is invariant under a uniform scale, so no
colour-space round trip and no per-colour fudge is needed; a separate "saturation/value mapping" is **not**. R078's quoted (99,131,172) was
an AA pixel — the cores are what settle it. (2026-10-17)

## 本轮 (R079)
Atomic step: **E01/E02 step 3 — `timedChip`'s Label `color:` `AppTheme.text` → a derived `inkColor`.** Edit
(`apps/calendar/qml/CalendarScheduleView.qml:626-646` + the Label): `readonly property color inkColor` = `c + (pole − c) * 0.5` with
`pole = AppTheme.dark ? 1 : 0`. Evidence: `docs/ui-calendar/r079-ink-light.png`, `r079-ink-dark.png`, `r079-ink-compare.png`
(ref blue chip | ours, both ×3 NEAREST).
**How it was verified — a coverage model was needed, and the numbers are the proof.** A pixelSize-9 glyph never reaches full coverage,
so each chip was tested by **solving the blend's coverage per channel**: `t = (fill − pixel) / (fill − predicted ink)`. A correct ink makes
the three t's **agree**; a wrong one cannot.
- **Light:** green bar (57,196,135) → ink (28,98,67): darkest pixel (45,111,85) ⇒ t = 0.91/0.91/0.89. Gold (215,166,44) → (107,83,22):
  (129,105,43) ⇒ 0.84/0.86/0.89. Blue (48,140,198) → (24,70,99): (49,89,121) ⇒ 0.87/0.88/0.85.
- **Dark:** green → (156,226,195): (141,210,176) ⇒ 0.87/0.88/0.85. Gold → (235,211,150): (220,199,128) ⇒ 0.89/0.91/0.81. Blue →
  (151,197,226): (137,183,206) ⇒ 0.88/0.89/0.85.
**Nine chip readings, both legs, t agreeing to ±0.05 inside each pixel ⇒ the assumed endpoint is the ink.** Corroboration by kind: R078's
grey ink produced near-equal channels; every chip now reads **its own hue** (blue B>G>R, green G>B>R, gold R>G>B), which is the ref's
idiom, and the ×3 composite puts the ref's "Stretchin…" ink beside our "Morning planning" — same dark same-hue ink on a light same-hue wash.
